an5.22:1.1: “(1) Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is irreverent and undeferential, and his behavior is uncongenial to his fellow monks, it is impossible for him to fulfill the factor of proper conduct.
an5.22:1.2: (2) Without fulfilling the factor of proper conduct, it is impossible for him to fulfill the factor of a trainee.
an5.22:1.3: (3) Without fulfilling the factor of a trainee, it is impossible for him to fulfill the aggregate of virtuous behavior.
an5.22:1.4: (4) Without fulfilling the aggregate of virtuous behavior, it is impossible for him to fulfill the aggregate of concentration.
an5.22:1.5: (5) Without fulfilling the aggregate of concentration, it is impossible for him to fulfill the aggregate of wisdom.
an5.22:2.1: “(1) But, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is reverential and deferential, and his behavior is congenial to his fellow monks, it is possible for him to fulfill the factor of proper conduct.
an5.22:2.2: (2) Having fulfilled the factor of proper conduct, it is possible for him to fulfill the factor of a trainee.
an5.22:2.3: (3) Having fulfilled the factor of a trainee, it is possible for him to fulfill the aggregate of virtuous behavior.
an5.22:2.4: (4) Having fulfilled the aggregate of virtuous behavior, it is possible for him to fulfill the aggregate of concentration.
an5.22:2.5: (5) Having fulfilled the aggregate of concentration, it is possible for him to fulfill the aggregate of wisdom.”
